# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Skyler Alvarez**
Member ID: W485219153
[Street Address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Cigna — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE:** Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-21
**Reference number:** POC-8B473A1D50-39674
**Member:** Skyler Alvarez — **Member ID:** W485219153
**Service denied:** Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827
**Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), South Carolina
**Governing policy:** Cigna CMM-315 Shoulder Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026 — https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-315%20Shoul%20Surg%20Arthro%20%26%20Open%20Proc_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of my rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827) and asking Cigna to reconsider that decision and authorize the surgery. The notice dated 2026-08-21 states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am writing because my MRI report and my treatment records appear to line up directly with the criteria in the plan's own policy, quoted below. My surgeon, Reyes, MD (orthopedic surgery), has documented that this procedure is needed.

## The plan's own criteria, and what my records show

**1. Imaging findings — the reason given for the denial**

The plan's policy states:

> "MRI or CT shows EITHER of the following findings:
> ◦ Grade 2 or 3 partial-thickness rotator cuff tear (Ellman classification)
> ◦ full-thickness rotator cuff tear (Cofield classification)"

My records establish this. My MRI of the shoulder on 2026-07-13 showed a **full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm**, with grade 2 fatty atrophy. A full-thickness rotator cuff tear is the second of the two findings the policy accepts, and only one of the two is required.

**2. Symptoms**

The plan's policy states:

> "Symptoms include function-limiting pain (e.g., loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment)"

My records establish this. I have had 12 months of progressive shoulder pain that is not relieved by rest. I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height, and I cannot sleep on the affected side.

**3. Physical examination**

The plan's policy states:

> "Physical exam demonstrates BOTH of the following findings (as compared to the non- involved side):"

and, for the first of those two findings:

> "EITHER of the following findings:
> ▪ functionally-limited range of motion
> ▪ measurable loss of strength of the rotator cuff musculature"

My records state that my range of motion is limited by pain, which addresses the first of these two alternatives.

For the second finding, the policy lists a number of accepted tests, including:

> "ANY of the following positive orthopedic tests/signs:
> ▪ drop arm test
> ▪ painful arc test
> ▪ Jobe test or empty can test
> ▪ lateral Jobe test
> ▪ external rotation lag sign (dropping sign)
> ▪ external rotation resistance test
> ▪ full can test
> ▪ hug up test
> ▪ internal rotation lag sign"

and further:

> "▪ internal resistance rotation test (IRRT)
> ▪ internal rotation resistance test at maximal 90° of abduction and maximal external rotation test (IRRTM)
> ▪ lift-off test
> ▪ bear hug test
> ▪ belly press test (Napoleon)
> ▪ belly-off test
> ▪ Neer impingement test
> ▪ Hawkins-Kennedy impingement test
> ▪ Hornblower test (Patte)
> ▪ Yocum test"

My exam records state that provocative testing was positive on the affected side. So that the file is complete on this point, I am asking my surgeon's office to supply the named test or tests that were positive and the side-to-side comparison the policy describes: [names of positive orthopedic tests and side-to-side exam findings, to be supplied from Dr. Reyes's office notes].

**4. Non-surgical management**

The plan's policy states:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration"

My records establish this, and more. I completed **supervised physical therapy from 2026-03-25 to 2026-07-01 — 14 weeks and 16 visits**, focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, documented in the physical therapy discharge note. I also took NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-12 that gave only about 3 weeks of partial relief.

I want to address one related point directly, because it works in favor of coverage here rather than against it. The policy provides:

> "Criteria exception: Three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management is not required for an individual who suffers a discrete traumatic event that results in an acute full-thickness rotator cuff tear without evidence of a pre-existing chronic rotator cuff tear."

and:

> "Note: The presence of fatty infiltration and/or muscle atrophy on MRI or CT is considered evidence of a pre-existing chronic rotator cuff tear."

and:

> "Therefore, when fatty infiltration and/or muscle atrophy is also present on MRI or CT, three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management is required, regardless of whether a discrete traumatic event occurred."

My MRI shows grade 2 fatty atrophy, so I am not relying on the criteria exception. My records show provider-directed non-surgical management over an extended period: supervised physical therapy from 2026-03-25 to 2026-07-01 (14 weeks, 16 visits), NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-12 that gave only about 3 weeks of partial relief.

**5. Other conditions excluded**

The plan's policy also states:

> "Other potential pathological conditions have been excluded, including, but not limited to the following: fracture, thoracic outlet syndrome, brachial plexus disorders, referred neck pain, cervical radiculopathy, and advanced glenohumeral osteoarthritis."

My records note no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and that I am a non-smoker. For completeness on this criterion, my surgeon's office can provide the documentation of alternative diagnoses considered and ruled out: [documentation of excluded conditions from Dr. Reyes's office notes].

## A note on the criteria I was given

The excerpts above are the policy language I have. One of them ends in a colon and introduces material I do not have in front of me, and the policy may contain additional requirements that were not reproduced for me. **I am asking Cigna to identify in writing the specific criterion or criteria from Cigna CMM-315 Shoulder Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026 that my request was found not to meet**, and, if the denial rests on the imaging, to explain how a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm on the 2026-07-13 MRI does not satisfy the imaging criterion quoted above. Anything I have not put in quotation marks in this letter is my own description and not the plan's wording.

## What I am requesting

I ask that Cigna overturn the determination dated 2026-08-21 (reference POC-8B473A1D50-39674) and authorize rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827, as requested by Dr. Reyes. I am happy to have any additional records sent, and I ask that this appeal be reviewed by a physician with expertise in orthopedic shoulder surgery.

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-02-17** (180 days from the date of the notice). I am submitting it through my.cigna.com using my plan's appeal form, or to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; I can also be reached by phone if anything further is needed, and I understand I may call 1-800-244-6224 or the number on my card with questions.

**Enclosed:**
- Copy of the denial notice dated 2026-08-21
- MRI report of the shoulder, 2026-07-13
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-25 to 2026-07-01, 16 visits)
- Office notes from Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery
- [Any additional records, e.g., injection record of 2026-05-12]

Thank you for taking another look at this.

Sincerely,

​
_______________________________
**Skyler Alvarez**
